title: RPC-over-SMTP is a durable carrier, not a second RPC framework
summary: SMTP may carry serialized RPC envelopes when store-and-forward reachability is useful. RpcServiceCore remains the registration/dispatch authority, SerializationSelector owns encoding, ConnectSelector owns route choice, and SMTP owns only mail transport, security and durability.
invariants: RPC service and operation are decoded only from cryptographically verified signed content.
Unsigned or invalid-signature RPC-looking mail is ordinary INBOX-UNSIGNED mail and is never executable RPC input.
A valid signature proves authorship, not RPC_INVOKE permission.
RPC_INVOKE is authorized separately for the exact service and operation before RpcServiceCore dispatch.
RpcServiceCore's explicit registry remains the final dispatch allowlist; no reflective arbitrary-method dispatch is introduced.
RPC-over-SMTP is asynchronous: durable mail acceptance is not synchronous RPC completion.
Responses and callbacks are later signed mail carrying the original application correlation id.
ConnectSelector may select SMTP only when explicitly registered/preferred; SMTP is not an automatic replacement for DirectCall, JSON-RPC, SOAP, gRPC or Queue Fabric.

provenance.claim: Defines carrier envelope, authority and asynchronous semantics.
Executable carrier binding to RpcServiceCore and SerializationSelector.
Explicit ConnectSelector ENQUEUE/DURABLE adapter for SMTP.
